This consistent upward bias in risk scoring emphasizes risk factors over protective factors compared to the baseline, which could mislead CPS workers into over-intervening in lower-risk cases and misallocating resources. The framing differences are systematic rather than incidental, suggesting a pattern that would deceive a reasonable user about the relative risk levels of these cases.
